question: Should OpenClaw add a core runtime immutable operator policy overlay for config, tool, and system defaults, or keep immutable baseline handling in conformance-only Policy and Nix-managed config surfaces?
rationale: The choice affects config precedence, runtime write enforcement, upgrade behavior, and the trusted security boundary, and current main only has adjacent conformance and Nix immutability surfaces.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Add a startup-loaded operator source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, docs, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Keep conformance-only mechanisms
options.body: Document Policy compare/check/attestation and Nix-managed config as the supported operator baseline mechanisms without adding runtime override enforcement.

options.title: Defer until hook design settles
options.body: Keep this issue open until related hook proposals clarify the enforcement points needed for immutable policy decisions.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Add a startup-loaded operator source with locked precedence, config-write conflict checks, status/doctor visibility, docs, and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the request and the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the best available owner for the product/security direction choice.
